questions.stem: Under the Constitution of India, who officially holds the power to appoint the Chief Justice of India and the other judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Article 124(2) states that every Judge of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. In practice, the President acts on the binding recommendation of the Supreme Court Collegium.

questions.stem: What is the mandatory, constitutionally prescribed retirement age for a sitting judge of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: A judge of the Supreme Court holds office until they attain the age of 65 years. In contrast, the retirement age for a judge of a State High Court is 62 years.

questions.stem: Under which specific Article of the Constitution can the President of India seek the official advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or public importance?
questions.explanation: Article 143 grants the Supreme Court 'Advisory Jurisdiction'. If the President believes a question of law or fact has arisen that is of public importance, he may refer the question to the Supreme Court for its consideration.

questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of the Supreme Court (and High Courts) to examine the constitutionality of legislative and executive actions.
